content_units: Best-Fit Laptop Snapshot
For architecture study plus light video editing under   1,400 EUR  , the best value is   Laptop C   if you want the strongest all-around balance of battery, portability, RAM headroom, and storage.
If display quality for visual work matters most and shorter battery life is acceptable,   Laptop B   is the performance-focused alternative.
Laptop Comparison Table
Model   Price   Weight   Battery   RAM / Storage   Display   Graphics   Fit for your priorities
Laptop A     1,299 EUR       1.24 kg       18 hrs     16 GB / 512 GB   13.6-inch   Integrated   Best portability and battery, but weaker for architecture workloads and limited storage
Laptop B     1,379 EUR     1.8 kg   8 hrs   16 GB / 1 TB     15.6-inch OLED       RTX 4050     Best display and graphics power, but heaviest and weakest battery
Laptop C     1,349 EUR     1.45 kg   12 hrs     32 GB / 1 TB     14-inch IPS   Integrated   Best balance of battery, RAM, storage, and commuting comfort
Value Recommendation for Architecture Students
Option 1:   Laptop C     Best overall value for a student who commutes and needs long-term usability     32 GB RAM + 12 hr battery
Why it stands out:
-   32 GB RAM   is a major advantage for architecture apps, large files, multitasking, and light editing timelines.
-   1.45 kg   is still very manageable for daily commuting.
-   12-hour battery   is comfortably better than Laptop B and more practical for campus use.
-   1 TB SSD   gives better room for project files, Adobe caches, renders, and asset libraries.
- The main trade-off is   integrated graphics  , so it is better for   light   rather than heavy 3D rendering.
Option 2:   Laptop B     Best if GPU acceleration and display quality matter more than mobility     OLED + RTX 4050
Why you might choose it instead:
-   RTX 4050   will help most with 3D modeling, rendering previews, GPU-accelerated creative apps, and smoother editing.
-   OLED display   is likely the most color-accurate and visually impressive of the three.
-   1 TB SSD   is also strong for media/project work.
Why it is not the best value for your priorities:
-   8-hour battery   is the weakest here.
-   1.8 kg   is noticeably heavier for commuting.
- It only matches the minimum RAM target at   16 GB  , while Laptop C exceeds it.
Option 3:   Laptop A     Best ultra-portable pick, but the least suitable for architecture growth     1.24 kg + 18 hr battery
Where it wins:
- Easiest to carry every day.
- Strongest battery life by far.
- Lowest price of the three.
Why it falls behind:
-   Integrated graphics   and   512 GB SSD   make it less future-proof for architecture software and editing files.
- At   13.6 inches  , screen workspace may feel tight for CAD, drawings, and timeline-based editing.
- It meets the minimum RAM requirement, but does not offer the headroom Laptop C does.
Student Workload Fit
For architecture software
-   Laptop B   is strongest for GPU-assisted workflows and heavier 3D use.
-   Laptop C   is better for general architecture study, drafting, multitasking, and moderate creative work.
-   Laptop A   is more suitable for lighter coursework than demanding architecture projects.
For light video editing
-   Laptop B   will export faster and handle effects better.
-   Laptop C   should still perform well for light edits because   32 GB RAM   helps a lot with multitasking and timeline responsiveness.
-   Laptop A   is the most constrained due to storage and likely lower sustained graphics performance.
For commuting and battery
-   Laptop A   wins clearly.
-   Laptop C   is the best compromise.
-   Laptop B   is the least convenient for all-day campus use.
Best Buy Under 1,400 EUR
Recommended: Laptop C
It best matches your priority order:
-   Battery life:   good at 12 hrs
-   16 GB RAM minimum:   exceeds this with   32 GB
-   Color-accurate display:   IPS can be good, though not as strong as B’s OLED
-   Not too heavy:     1.45 kg   is reasonable for daily commuting
Why it is the best value:

For only   50 EUR more than Laptop A  , you get   double the RAM  ,   double the storage  , and still keep solid portability and battery life. Compared with Laptop B, you give up dedicated graphics and OLED, but gain much better mobility and battery for student life.
Context for the Recommendation
Because no exact brightness, color gamut, or CPU details were provided, this recommendation assumes:
- the IPS panel on Laptop C is at least decent quality for student design work,
- your video editing is light rather than professional-grade,
- your architecture workload is mixed coursework rather than constant heavy rendering.
